meta.title: A Hot Day at the Market Cafe
meta.textType: a menu with pictures and prices

paragraphs: I am May, and I am eleven years old. On Saturday, Grandma takes Pat and me to the market. It is a hot day, and the temperature is thirty-four degrees. We are hungry, so we stop at a cafe in the middle of the market. The cafe is near the west gate, next to a small college. Students sit at the tables and read books. A menu with pictures is on the table. Our dad works at the market too, but he is busy today. The market is full of people and noise.

I read the menu to Pat. The pictures look very good. Noodle soup is forty baht. Fried rice is fifty baht. Papaya salad is thirty baht. Iced tea is twenty baht. Hot tea is fifteen baht. Coconut water is twenty baht too. "I can't decide," says Pat.

"Do you prefer rice or noodles?" asks Grandma. "I prefer rice," says Pat. "Then take the fried rice," I say. "The day is hot, so I want a cold drink," says Pat. "Take the coconut water," I say. Grandma prefers a hot drink on a hot day. She orders noodle soup and hot tea.

I write a note for the waiter. "Grandma: noodle soup and hot tea. Pat: fried rice and coconut water. May: papaya salad and iced tea." The waiter reads it and nods. He puts the note in his pocket. The food comes fast. Pat eats his rice with a big spoon. He eats all of it. Then he asks for a glass of water. My papaya salad is a little hot, so I drink my iced tea. Grandma smiles and says, "A good lunch!"
text.summary: May, Pat, and Grandma have lunch at a cafe in the middle of the market. May reads the menu and the prices, and she writes a note about what each person orders.
